reader.notes: PAGE-COUNTER receiving references go through ResolveReceiving to CounterPlace, a place on the report's own register, which the runtime engine reads and increments, so an altered value carries into later page headings. The register holds more than 999999 with no size error, which the 1985 'must be capable of representing' wording permits.

refuter.evidence: Receiving contexts and values the reader did not run, from pc_more_contexts at 85: STRING POINTER, UNSTRING COUNT IN and TALLYING IN, SEARCH VARYING, and SET PAGE-COUNTER TO index-name each store into the counter (5, 2, 2, 4, 3). The implicit description is an unsigned integer (§1985:XIII.1.2.2). MOVE -5 stores 5 (NEG=0000005), and SUBTRACT 10 FROM 3 stores 7 (SUBNEG=0000007), the absolute value for an unsigned receiver. MOVE 7.9 truncates to 7, and COMPUTE ROUNDED = 7.6 gives 8. In n_one_global_unq, a contained program's ADD 1 TO an unqualified global PAGE-COUNTER is seen by the container (41). The reader's run of the altered value carrying into the next page heading stands. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.5.5 SR6  (3.5.5 PAGE-COUNTER Rules)  the text is in SR6'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.1.2.2 ...'.
